label: copy-phase fed-back f, mostly when the next output is h
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, nearly always (97% of mass) when the fed-back input is f; a small remainder is on input h, mostly where the next output is h too (h h pairs). It fires on only about 8% of copy-phase f inputs. Which ones depends on the token being output right after f: h gets 46% of mass (activation precision 0.63 for f->h), then f, n, x, 0, 1. The largest activations (up to 3.3) are f followed by h at recall positions 2-4 in long sequences. Never fires in the original or delimiter phase, at recall positions 0-1, or on any other input token. Within copy-phase f, the predicate based on the output token reaches about 0.33 precision and 0.64 recall (0.77 mass), so the selectivity is only partly captured.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token (most: f, h, x, -, z, 0; least: q, d, s, 2) and the token being output (most: h, f, n, 1, x, 0; least: w, -, a, t); timing cues that raise it most: recall_idx=3, recall_idx=4, t=12.
